name: beyond_add_transformation_by_sql
description: SQL is BE data-flow notation across all relevant layers, including React UI, Controller, Service and integration; runtime SQL is not required. Read transformation_design_guide. Review relevant processor flows, not only DAO/Repository. Parse a SQL SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE statement into one transformation and persist it for the target processor. INSERT into processor INPUT maps all argument sources directly in one transformation, preserving expressions without intermediate OUTPUT/LOOKUP, for Controller and Service regardless of use_lookup. Literals have no fabricated source. Local arguments are not response fields. Storage-entity INSERT maps simple caller values directly; other expressions may materialize caller OUTPUT. Processor destinations must be existing INPUT attributes; do not fall back to OUTPUT/LOOKUP with the same name. Explicit target attribute IDs remain authoritative. Missing or ambiguous destination attributes fail before writes. Existing transformations and historical ports are not automatically rewritten or deleted. Controller INSERT rejects mixed endpoint handlers even for direct callee INPUT mappings. For storage-entity destinations, one handler INPUT combined with storage-entity values, literals or expressions maps directly without fabricated OUTPUT fields. Mixed handlers are rejected; other source scopes require a verified handler OUTPUT contract. Infer the handler only from resolved contract attribute IDs, or specify AS "handler.field" (required when no handler can be inferred). The destination column selects the same-named child unless an explicit handler path is given. Never create or reuse a top-level Controller OUTPUT for this purpose. Mixed handlers, missing fields, or ambiguous contracts fail before writes. Direct caller-attribute handoffs still need no intermediate OUTPUT. Do not invent response fields solely to make SQL succeed. For automatic LOOKUP/OUTPUT targets, direct references retain source type, length and precision. Inherit the source logical name only when the target column name equals the source column name; a different AS alias becomes the new logical name. Expressions use their result alias without inheriting argument dimensions. INSERT ports retain destination metadata. Existing attributes keep their IDs and user-defined names. Top-level SELECT UNION, UNION ALL and UNION DISTINCT are supported: columns map by position to the first SELECT output names, and all branches feed the same target attribute IDs. Branch predicates and join definitions are preserved in other_info.sql_set_operation, not combined as global filters. Raw SQL retains UNION duplicate semantics; BE records lineage and does not execute SQL. INTERSECT, EXCEPT, nested or parenthesized compound queries, aggregate/GROUP BY branches, INSERT with a compound SELECT, and compound ORDER BY/LIMIT/OFFSET/FETCH are not supported; SQL_UNSUPPORTED explains the boundary. For these cases use separate branch transformations with the same output aliases when that accurately represents the design. The SQL should be a single statement and should keep request inputs as named placeholders such as :customerId, :coupon_id, :query_embedding, :size, and :status so they can be resolved against processor INPUT attributes. Do not inline user/request values. SELECT parsing supports vector distance expressions such as d.embedding <-> :query_embedding and COSINE_DISTANCE(d.embedding, :query_embedding) in projections, JOIN predicates, WHERE threshold filters, and ORDER BY clauses; those transformations use semantic_level='VECTOR'. Boolean vector threshold projections such as d.embedding <-> :query_embedding < 0.8 use projection_type='VECTOR_COMPARISON'. In SQL-to-transformation conversion, object names in SQL may refer to database tables, file entities, Redis structures, or processors. When a processor is referenced in SQL, treat its INPUT/LOOKUP/OUTPUT attributes as columns. Use SELECT ... AS target_column_name to disambiguate duplicate column names or separate same-named UI fields. Avoid bare SELECT column names when multiple source attributes share the same column_name. Automatic target_column_name creation creates flat top-level LOOKUP attributes; pre-create nested LOOKUP/OUTPUT targets when object/array lineage must be preserved. The response includes auto_created_attributes and auto_created_attribute_ids when this tool creates attributes; do not create those attributes again. Do not invent conceptual intermediate names such as extract_row, transformed_row, payload, document_row, or source_doc unless those objects are actually modeled. If parsing fails, correct the SQL or model schema and retry this tool. Preserve the actual BE physical name. Quote names containing punctuation, spaces, or dots with backticks or double quotes; for example FROM `qwen3-4b:Q4_K_M` AS m or FROM "chat:session:{sessionId}:info" m. Never rename an object merely to make SQL parse. Escape an embedded quote by doubling that quote. Quoted identifiers are atomic: :, -, ., {}, and whitespace remain part of the name. "model.onnx" is one physical name; schema.table is a qualified name. Single quotes denote string literals, not object names. Colons in quoted identifiers or string literals do not create bind parameters. Use FROM object alias or FROM object AS alias, then alias.column. Attribute names can also be quoted. Sources may belong to any accessible model, not only the processor model. When names collide, use model_id."physical_name" (the model name or schema name is also accepted if unique). Do not guess a candidate. The error lists accessible candidates; an incorrect qualifier does not fall back to an unqualified name. Use FROM BE_OBJECT('entity_id') AS m for explicit object-ID references. A bare ent_... token is still a name, never an inferred ID. Name-based and ID-based references apply the same canvas access checks. Stored transformations and lineage reference object and attribute IDs and survive renames; saved raw SQL is not rewritten automatically. SQL_SYNTAX, SQL_OBJECT_NOT_FOUND, SQL_ATTRIBUTE_NOT_FOUND, SQL_AMBIGUOUS_OBJECT, SQL_AMBIGUOUS_ATTRIBUTE, and SQL_ACCESS_DENIED distinguish failures. Resolve them using the latest MCP schema. A failed single SQL conversion must not create partial attributes or transformations. Respect storage-type use_lookup. When false, new targets use OUTPUT; explicit LOOKUP targets fail. Controller nested response fields must exist first: AS "handler.field"; read sources with alias.OUTPUT.handler.field. Parameterless SQL reads also create caller-to-source object-level QUERY_PARAMETER dependencies; undefined bind parameters fail. Do not omit verified calls because request data is absent. This does not provide general execution/DDL lineage: document unsupported pure calls and DDL with caller/target, condition and code evidence. Never invent fields or SELECT 1 to draw a connection. In-memory responses may still have processor-to-field lineage without a backing store. Caller INPUT binds support :handler.field and :INPUT.handler.field. Read controller_sql_input_guide via beyond_get_definitions for self-alias and mixed storage INSERT examples.

processor_id.description: The ID of the processor executing the logic.

sql.description: Single SQL statement to convert into a transformation. Keep request inputs as named placeholders like :customerId, :coupon_id, :query_embedding, :page, :size, or :status instead of replacing them with concrete values. Vector distance SQL such as d.embedding <-> :query_embedding, d.embedding <#> c.embedding, or COSINE_DISTANCE(d.embedding, :query_embedding) can be used in SELECT, JOIN, WHERE, and ORDER BY. SQL object names may refer to tables, files, Redis structures, or processors. Use SELECT ... AS target_column_name for duplicate field names and UI-region-specific target names. Automatic target_column_name creation is flat; create nested target attributes first when list/object lineage must be preserved. If the response lists auto_created_attributes, do not create those attributes separately. Do not send pseudo-SQL or API payload text such as Elasticsearch _bulk bodies. Do not use imaginary intermediate source names unless they are modeled objects. Preserve the actual BE physical name. Quote names containing punctuation, spaces, or dots with backticks or double quotes; for example FROM `qwen3-4b:Q4_K_M` AS m or FROM "chat:session:{sessionId}:info" m. Never rename an object merely to make SQL parse. Escape an embedded quote by doubling that quote. Quoted identifiers are atomic: :, -, ., {}, and whitespace remain part of the name. "model.onnx" is one physical name; schema.table is a qualified name. Single quotes denote string literals, not object names. Colons in quoted identifiers or string literals do not create bind parameters. Use FROM object alias or FROM object AS alias, then alias.column. Attribute names can also be quoted. Sources may belong to any accessible model, not only the processor model. When names collide, use model_id."physical_name" (the model name or schema name is also accepted if unique). Do not guess a candidate. The error lists accessible candidates; an incorrect qualifier does not fall back to an unqualified name. Use FROM BE_OBJECT('entity_id') AS m for explicit object-ID references. A bare ent_... token is still a name, never an inferred ID. Name-based and ID-based references apply the same canvas access checks. Stored transformations and lineage reference object and attribute IDs and survive renames; saved raw SQL is not rewritten automatically.

transformation_name.description: Optional name for the created transformation. Defaults to a SQL-derived label.

processing_order.description: Optional processing order. If omitted, the server appends the transformation after existing ones.

auto_created_attributes.description: Flattened list of attributes automatically created while adding these transformations. Do not create these attributes again.

auto_created_attribute_ids.description: Flattened IDs of attributes automatically created while adding these transformations.

auto_created_attribute_summary.description: Attribute automatically created while persisting a transformation. The client should not create this attribute again.

created_for.description: Why the attribute was created, such as projections.target_attribute, aggregations.target_attribute, or source_attributes.lookup.

auto_created_attributes.description: Attributes automatically created while adding this transformation. Do not create these attributes again.

auto_created_attribute_ids.description: IDs of attributes automatically created while adding this transformation.
